key_insight: Selecting retrieval-pipeline configurations per query (LLM, retriever, docs, hops, synthesis) lets systems meet accuracy or budget targets more efficiently than static, hand-tuned pipelines.
problem_solved: Static, one-size-fits-all retrieval pipelines waste cost or miss accuracy opportunities; the paper enables per-query configuration selection to optimize cost or accuracy given a user target.
method: Formulate the task: map (natural-language query + target: accuracy or budget) to a choice from a predefined pipeline catalog.
Learn or predict per-config cost and accuracy for a query, then select the configuration that satisfies the target while minimizing cost (or maximizing accuracy under a budget).
Evaluate selection across workloads to demonstrate per-query tuning reduces serving cost and/or improves answer quality compared to fixed pipelines.
impact: Practitioners can reduce serving costs and improve end-user accuracy by automatically adapting retrieval-agent pipelines per query, enabling scalable, cost-aware deployment of LLM-backed retrieval systems.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Query + target → selector → chosen pipeline (showing LLM, retriever, docs, hops, synthesis components).
Cost vs. Accuracy scatter with Pareto frontier: per-query points showing dynamic selection outperforms fixed pipelines.
Before/After bar chart: average serving cost and accuracy for static pipeline vs. per-query configured pipeline.
Icons: LLM, search/retriever, document stack, dollar/coin, and accuracy gauge to annotate pipeline components and objectives.
paper_title: Natural Language Query to Configuration for Retrieval Agents
paper_authors: Melissa Z. Pan, Negar Arabzadeh, Mathew Jacob, Fiodar Kazhamiaka, Esha Choukse
